h1: How to Set Up a Restaurant Instagram That Turns Followers Into Diners
metaTitle: How to Set Up a Restaurant Instagram (Beginner Guide)
metaDescription: A plain-English, click-by-click guide on how to set up a restaurant Instagram: switch to a free Business account, write a bio that drives visits, and more.
heroAlt: A restaurant's Instagram profile displayed on a phone
directAnswer: To set up a restaurant Instagram, open the app, go to your profile, tap the menu, and switch to a free professional Business account under Settings and privacy, then Account type and tools. Write a bio that names your food, your neighborhood, and one clear next step. Add your address and contact buttons under Edit profile, turn on an action button like Reserve or Order food, and point your link in bio to your menu and reservations. Finish by building Story Highlights for your menu, hours, and specials, then publish your first posts.
keyTakeaways: A Business account is free and unlocks the tools that turn a visitor into a customer: contact buttons, an action button, and insights.
Switch in about five minutes: profile, the three lines menu, Settings and privacy, Account type and tools, Switch to professional account, then choose Business.
Write a bio that says what you serve, where you are, and one next step, and put your Miami neighborhood in it so nearby people find you.
Add your address and contact buttons under Edit profile, then turn on one action button (Reserve for tables, Order food for delivery or pickup).

Build Story Highlights for Menu, Hours, and Specials, then publish your first posts: your signature dish, your space, your story, and your hours.
intro:
You spend an hour styling a plate, snap the photo, post it, and get a handful of likes from people who live three states away. Meanwhile the family that just moved in around the corner never finds you. That gap, between a pretty feed and a full dining room, is where most restaurant Instagram accounts get stuck.

Here is the good news. Instagram already sends you ready-to-eat customers. Someone searches a neighborhood, taps a food photo, lands on a profile, and decides in about ten seconds whether to come in. Whether they walk through your door comes down to a few settings most owners never turn on.

This guide sets up your restaurant Instagram the right way, click by click, so the account does more than collect likes. You do not need any marketing background. If you can send a photo in a text message, you can do every step here.

sections.h2: What is an Instagram Business account, and why does your restaurant need one?
sections.html:
Let us start with the one distinction that matters. Instagram has two kinds of accounts. A personal account is what most people sign up with. A professional account is the free upgrade built for businesses, and it comes in two flavors: Business and Creator. For a restaurant, you want Business.

Switching costs nothing. There is no monthly fee and no catch. What you get is the set of tools that quietly turns a curious scroller into a paying guest: contact buttons (call, email, and directions to your door), an action button (like Reserve or Order food) that sits right at the top of your profile, and insights, which is simply Instagram's word for the numbers that show which posts brought people in.

Here is why this matters for a restaurant in Miami. When a tourist in Wynwood or a family in Doral is deciding where to eat, they often check your Instagram before your website. If your profile shows a beautiful plate but no address, no hours, and no way to book, they bounce to the spot next door that made it easy. A Business account is how you make it easy.

sections.h2: How do you switch to a free Business account, step by step?
sections.html:
This takes about five minutes and it is reversible, so you can switch back anytime. Do it on your phone, where the option is easiest to find.

  1. Open the Instagram app and tap your profile picture in the bottom right corner to open your profile.
  2. Tap the three horizontal lines in the top right corner (that is the menu).
  3. Tap Settings and privacy.
  4. Scroll to the section for professionals (it may be labeled Your insights and tools or For professionals) and tap Account type and tools.
  5. Tap Switch to professional account, then tap Continue through the short welcome screens.
  6. Pick the category that fits you best, like Restaurant, Bar, or Cafe, and choose whether to display it on your profile.
  7. When Instagram asks you to choose an account type, tap Business (not Creator), then tap Next.
  8. Instagram will offer to connect a Facebook Page. This is optional, so you can skip it now and link one later if you have one.

Two things to know. First, professional accounts are always public, so if your profile was private, Instagram will make it public and accept any pending follow requests. That is what you want anyway. Second, on a computer you can do the same thing: go to instagram.com, click More in the left sidebar, click Settings, find the For professionals section, and follow the same steps.

sections.h2: How do you write a bio that turns a visit into a reservation?
sections.html:
Your bio is the short block of text under your name at the top of your profile. You get about 150 characters, and it is the first thing a stranger reads. Most restaurants waste it on a slogan nobody remembers. Yours should answer three questions fast: what do you serve, where are you, and what should I do next.

Before the bio itself, fix your Name field. That is the bold line at the very top, and it is different from your @username. Instagram lets people search that Name field, so put real words in it, not just your brand. Casa Lola alone is a missed chance. Casa Lola | Cuban Restaurant Miami helps you show up when someone searches Cuban food nearby.

Then write the bio using a simple recipe:

  1. What you serve, in plain words. For example, Wood-fired pizza and natural wine.
  2. Where you are, with the neighborhood. For example, In the heart of Little Havana. Naming a Miami neighborhood helps nearby people trust you are close.
  3. One next step, a short call to action that points at your link. For example, Book a table below or See tonight's menu below.

Keep it readable, use one or two emojis at most as visual markers (a slice, a pin), and skip the hashtags in your bio. Save those for posts.

sections.h2: How do you add your address and contact buttons?
sections.html:
This is the step that makes your profile useful instead of just pretty. Contact buttons appear as tappable options under your bio, so a hungry guest can call you, email you, or get driving directions with one tap.

  1. From your profile, tap Edit profile.
  2. Tap Contact options.
  3. Tap Business address and enter your street address, city, state, and ZIP code. When someone taps your location later, it opens their map app with directions to your door already loaded.
  4. Back in Contact options, add a phone number and a business email so the Call and Email buttons appear.
  5. Tap Save.

One more toggle to check. Still under Edit profile, look in the Public business information area for Profile display and make sure Display contact info is turned on. If it is off, your buttons stay hidden even after you fill everything in.

Instagram does not have a dedicated hours field the way Google does, so we will handle your hours with a Story Highlight further down. For now, get the address, phone, and email in place.

sections.h2: How do you add a Reserve or Order food action button?
sections.html:
An action button is the big button at the top of your profile that does one job: it lets a guest book a table or order food without leaving Instagram. You can have one action button at a time, so pick the one that matches how you make money.

  1. From your profile, tap Edit profile.
  2. Scroll to Public business information and tap Action buttons.
  3. Choose the button that fits you: Reserve to take table bookings, or Order food (sometimes shown as Start order) for delivery and pickup.
  4. Connect the partner you already use, or sign up with one. Reserve works with partners like OpenTable, Resy, and Yelp Reservations. Ordering works with partners like ChowNow and others.
  5. Follow the prompts to link your account, then tap Done. The button now sits at the top of your profile.

If you do not use a booking or ordering partner yet, do not force it. You can point people to your menu and reservations through your link in bio instead, which is the next step. A dead button is worse than no button.

sections.h2: What should your link in bio point to?
sections.html:
Your link in bio is the tappable web link on your profile. For years Instagram allowed only one, which is why you have heard the phrase so often. Now you can add up to five links natively, so you can send people exactly where they want to go.

  1. Tap Edit profile.
  2. Tap Links (older versions may say Website).
  3. Tap Add external link, paste the web address, and give it a clear title like See the Menu or Book a Table.
  4. Repeat to add more, up to five total. Drag to reorder, and put your most important link first, because Instagram shows the top one most prominently.
  5. Tap Done to save.

For a restaurant, a strong order is Menu, then Reserve, then Order online. Point the menu link at your own website (like yourrestaurant.com/menu) rather than a downloadable PDF, since a PDF is slow and hard to read on a phone. If you need more than five links, or you rotate offers a lot, you can use a free link-in-bio page, which is one link that opens a simple page holding all your buttons in one place.

sections.h2: How do you set up Story Highlights for your menu, hours, and specials?
sections.html:
A Story is a photo or video that disappears after 24 hours. A Highlight is a saved Story that stays on your profile forever, shown as a little circle under your bio. Highlights are how a first-time visitor answers their own questions (What is on the menu? When are you open? What is the special?) without messaging you.

Because a Highlight is built from Stories, you post a Story first, then save it. Here is the full flow:

  1. Post a Story for each topic. For example, take a photo of your printed menu, a simple card that lists your hours, and today's special, and share each one as a Story.
  2. Go to your profile and find the Highlights row just below your bio. Tap the circle that says New (or tap the plus in the top right corner and choose Story highlight).
  3. Select the Stories you want in this Highlight, then tap Next.
  4. Choose a cover image and type a short name like Menu, Hours, or Specials. Keep names to one word so they are not cut off.
  5. Tap Add. The Highlight now stays on your profile until you remove it.

Start with four Highlights: Menu, Hours, Specials, and Reviews. Use covers in the same color so your profile looks put together. When your menu or hours change, just post a new Story and add it to the matching Highlight, then delete the outdated one.

sections.h2: What are the first posts you should publish?
sections.html:
An empty grid makes a new visitor nervous. You do not need 30 posts, but you want enough that the profile looks alive and answers the question every diner has: is this place any good, and is it open. Aim to publish these first, spacing them over your first week or two.

  • Your signature dish. Lead with the thing people come for, shot in good natural light. This is your handshake.
  • Your space. A wide shot of the dining room or patio so people can picture themselves there. Miami diners care a lot about the vibe.
  • A short Reel of food being made. A Reel is a short vertical video. Instagram pushes Reels to people who do not follow you yet, so a 10 second clip of a dish coming together often reaches far more new locals than a photo.
  • Your hours and location. A simple, readable post that states when you are open and where you are, so nobody has to dig.
  • Your story. One post about who you are and why you opened. People root for the family behind the food.
  • A happy guest or a review. A photo of a full table or a screenshot of a kind review builds instant trust.

After that, a steady rhythm of a few posts a week keeps you visible far more than a burst once a month. If keeping up with posting on top of running the kitchen sounds like one job too many, that is normal, and it is exactly the kind of work our team handles for Miami restaurants through our restaurant social media service, from shooting the content to posting it on schedule.

faqs.q: How do I set up an Instagram for my restaurant?
faqs.a: Open the Instagram app, go to your profile, and switch to a free professional Business account through Settings and privacy, then Account type and tools, then Switch to professional account. Choose the Restaurant category and select Business. Then write a bio that names your food, neighborhood, and one next step, add your address and contact buttons under Edit profile, turn on an action button like Reserve or Order food, and set your link in bio to your menu and reservations. Finish by creating Story Highlights for your menu, hours, and specials, and publishing your first few posts.

faqs.q: Is an Instagram Business account free for restaurants?
faqs.a: Yes. Switching to an Instagram Business account is completely free, with no monthly fee. It unlocks contact buttons, an action button for reservations or orders, and insights that show which posts are working. Instagram makes money from optional ads you can choose to run later, but the Business account itself, and every setup step in this guide, costs nothing.

faqs.q: Should a restaurant use a Business or Creator account?
faqs.a: A restaurant should use a Business account, not a Creator account. Both are free professional accounts, but Business is designed for companies with a physical location and unlocks the address and contact buttons, the Reserve and Order food action buttons, and directions to your door. Creator accounts are built for individual influencers and public figures, so they lack the local business features a restaurant needs most.

faqs.q: How do I add a Reserve or Order food button to my restaurant's Instagram?
faqs.a: Go to your profile, tap Edit profile, scroll to Public business information, and tap Action buttons. Choose Reserve to take table bookings or Order food for delivery and pickup, then connect a partner service. Reserve works with partners like OpenTable, Resy, and Yelp Reservations, while ordering works with partners like ChowNow. You can have one action button at a time, and it appears at the top of your profile once connected.

faqs.q: How many links can I put in my Instagram bio?
faqs.a: You can add up to five links directly in your Instagram bio. Tap Edit profile, tap Links, then Add external link, and repeat for each one. You can drag to reorder them, and the first link shows most prominently, so put your most important destination first. For a restaurant, a good order is your menu, then reservations, then online ordering.

faqs.q: Do I need a Facebook Page to set up an Instagram Business account?
faqs.a: No. Connecting a Facebook Page is optional and not required to switch to an Instagram Business account. You can complete the entire setup, including your bio, contact buttons, action button, and Highlights, without a Facebook Page. If you already have one, you can link it later to make running ads and cross-posting easier, but it is not a requirement to get started.

faqs.q: What should a restaurant post first on Instagram?
faqs.a: Start with your signature dish, a wide shot of your dining room or patio, and a short Reel of food being made, since Reels reach people who do not follow you yet. Add a clear post with your hours and location, one post telling your story, and a photo of a happy table or a kind review. These first posts make the profile look alive and answer the two questions every diner has: is the food good, and are you open.
